Home Brief

Standing context for the Home screen redesign, R2 campaign. Read before designing in the Round One claude.ai/design project. This is a brief — facts, requirements, and open questions — not a layout proposal. Section 2 and 3 are a direct read of app/(tabs)/index.tsx as it ships today; sections 4–5 are binding constraints carried in from the charter and the logging round; sections 6–7 are for this round to resolve, not this document.

1What Home Is

Home is the landing tab — the first screen on launch and the one every session returns to. Its one-tap common case is starting, or resuming, today's workout.

Its job, in one line: where you are, and back to it in one tap. Everything else on the screen — program context, calendar, health — is secondary to that single act.

2States to Design

Five states, corrected against the real branches in index.tsx. in code means the branch exists and paints correctly today; new means the state has no Home-level implementation yet and must be designed from scratch.

StateCondition in index.tsxStatusNotes
(a) Active program, workout day program && def && todayTemplate in code The hero state. Renders program context, timeline, health, TodayCard (training-day variant: name, exercise count, "Start Workout"), calendar.
(b) Active program, rest day program && def && !todayTemplate in code TodayCard swaps to "Rest Day" + a rotating quote (one of 12 hardcoded strings, indexed by day-of-year) + an optional "up next" preview line naming the next training day.
(c) In-progress session exists No condition — not queried on Home new — #70 Confirmed gap. getInProgressSession exists in src/db/sessions.ts and is called by useWorkoutSession inside the Workout tab, but Home never calls it. If you start today's workout, background the app, and return to Home, the TodayCard still reads "Start Workout" — there is no resume affordance, no elapsed-time signal, nothing that surfaces the session unmissably. This state can coincide with either (a) or (b)'s scheduled day.
(d) No program !program || !def, and no pending completed-program card in code Empty state: glyph ring, "No Active Program" title, subtitle copy, "Browse Programs" button → /library. Health card and calendar still render underneath.
(e) Program complete !program || !def, plus a completed program with card_dismissed = 0 in code corrected The task brief for this round described "seen + dismissed" as sub-states of this card. That's not quite what the code does — see the callout below.

Correction on (e): Home only ever paints one program-complete state — the persistent CompletedProgramCard (name, date range, PR count, adherence %, "View full summary" / "Start a New Program"). It shows once completion_seen = 1 and while card_dismissed = 0.

completion_seen gates a one-time full-screen celebration at /program-complete?celebrate=1 — the first time a program completes, Home's loadData() redirects there immediately and renders nothing else that pass. That celebration screen is not a Home state at all; it's a bounce-through. Once seen, it never fires again for that program.

card_dismissed is not a user-facing "dismiss" on the card either — there is no dismiss control in CompletedProgramCard.tsx today. It flips to 1 automatically as a side effect of activating, restarting, or stopping a program elsewhere in the app. "Dismissed" isn't a look the card takes — it's the card's absence, falling through to whichever of (a)/(b)/(d) applies next.

Not listed as a designable state: the bare loading flash (if (loading) return <View style={styles.container} />) — an unstyled blank container shown for the duration of loadData(). Transient and not worth a state slot, but worth knowing it exists.

3Today's Content Inventory

Every section Home renders, in the order it renders, read from index.tsx and the components it imports (TodayCard, HealthCard, CompletedProgramCard, ProgramTimeline, MonthCalendar, FocusChips, PainFollowUp).

SectionData shownCondition / order
Wordmark header Chevron mark image (assets/logo-mark-small.png) + "PEX" set in Exo2 ExtraBold. Always first. Scrolls with content today — not pinned, not glass.
Settings gear Ionicons settings-outline, top-right of the header row. Always present. Navigates to /settings.
Program context Program name, FocusChips (focus tag pills from the program definition), "Week X of Y — [Block Name]" with the block name in the block's color. Active-program branch only (states a/b). First content under the header.
ProgramTimeline Horizontal segmented bar, one segment per training block, block-colored fills; the current block is brighter with a short label and an underline indicator. Active-program branch only. Directly under program context.
HealthCard Three-column bar: Sleep %, Recovery % (color-coded green/amber/red by score band), Strain — hairline dividers between columns. Renders in all three top-level branches whenever health data exists or is loading. Position shifts: after the timeline in the active-program branch, after the hero/empty/completed card in the other two.
PainFollowUp "How's the pain today?" prompt naming the run's date/duration/distance, an 11-point 0–10 pain selector with a hardcoded traffic-light color gradient, Save + a dismiss (×). Active-program branch only — never rendered in the no-program branch, even though the run it follows up on is logged independent of any program. Fires ~24h after a logged run.
TodayCard Training-day: label, session name, exercise count, "Start Workout" button — or, if completed, a checkmark badge + duration/set-count stats and the card becomes a link to the session detail. Rest-day: "Rest Day" title + rotating quote + optional "up next" line. Active-program branch only, always present (one of its two variants always applies). Does not distinguish a fresh start from a resume — see state (c).
MonthCalendar Full month grid with weekday header row, prev/next nav + swipe gesture, day circles color-coded (completed = filled green, today = outlined ring in the block color or a fallback, training days marked). Renders in all three top-level branches, always last. Loads month sessions even with no active program.
CompletedProgramCard Gold/amber top accent line, "✓ Completed" eyebrow, program name as hero text, date range + week count, hairline divider, PR count (amber) + adherence % (white) stats, "View full summary" and "Start a New Program" buttons. No-program branch only, state (e). Replaces the empty state when a completed, non-dismissed program exists.
Empty state Glyph ring (a 🏋 emoji), "No Active Program" title, subtitle copy, "Browse Programs" button. No-program branch, state (d) — no completed-program card pending.

No dead code found in index.tsx itself. Worth carrying into the redesign conversation: today's code alone uses at least five hues across these sections — the indigo accent (program context, timeline default, buttons), green (health recovery, completed badges), amber (completed-program card), cyan (PainFollowUp's border), plus the eleven-stop pain-severity gradient — well past the charter's two-hue budget. That's expected of pre-redesign code, not a bug to fix here, but it's the gap this round closes.

4What Binds This Screen (Already Locked)

  • Two hues, everything else neutral. Accent means now; moss means earned. If a third hue appears anywhere on Home, the design is wrong.
  • One light source, told twice at half strength — a halo behind the header, a vertical card gradient with a brighter top edge. Depth sums; it never stacks.
  • The biggest number wins. Hierarchy comes from numeral size and weight, never from color.
  • No vanity metrics. Every number on Home must be actionable or tell a story.
  • The bottom tab bar is always visible and glass — the R2 tab bar decision. It never hides on scroll.
  • Chrome-above-the-scroll wears glass; in-flow content is painted. One vocabulary, no exceptions: pinned nav sits in glass, everything that scrolls with the page is flat and hairline-bordered.
  • Floating glass controls must pass all three tests from the logging round: they sit over content that keeps moving, they're reachable without scrolling, and they're transient — appearing in response to something the user did, not living permanently on the screen. Floating glass should stay rare.
  • No em dashes anywhere in copy.
  • The wordmark is the chevron mark + "PEX" in Exo2 ExtraBold — the shipping face, not Orbitron.
  • The header grammar from logging is the established pattern wherever a header is needed: nav circles pinned, a large title live in the scroll flow, and a mini title fades into the pinned nav row past roughly 56px of scroll.

5Ben's Standing Taste (Recorded Feedback)

  • Health data is secondary, never hero. A compact text bar, not rings or gauges — Home's own HealthCard already leans this way; keep it that way, don't let it grow into a dashboard.
  • A card's action buttons live inside the card — grouped, matched in size to their siblings, text centered. No full-width edge-to-edge bars.
  • Muted and desaturated only. One or two hues maximum, roughly 60-30-10 in proportion. No neon, no multi-color decoration.

6Open Questions for This Round

  • ? The calendar carries two owner-verified jobs today: adherence at a glance (filled day-circles) and tap-a-day history access — his primary history-browsing path and the de-facto #63 entry point. This round must decide its form — inline week strip with expansion, icon-opened dedicated view, a hybrid, or the current inline month grid — but whichever form, both jobs must survive.
  • ? How much program context (block + week) does Home state directly, versus delegating to the Workout tab?
  • ? Where does settings live?
  • ? Does the wordmark header stay on Home?
  • ? What does the rest-day state lead with?
  • ? How loud should the #70 resume surface be?
